judge_output.rationale: No listed work measures the population correlation of fitted excess temperature with host luminosity, or searches for a luminosity-independent spike in the T_ex distribution, so the card's specific statistic is untested. Closely related claims have been tested, however. Hephaistos I (2022MNRAS.512.2988S) used Gaia-WISE colour cuts to set upper limits on the fraction of stars hosting fixed-temperature (100-1000 K, e.g. ~300 K) waste-heat components. Carrigan (2009ApJ...698.2075C) fitted 100-600 K blackbodies across IRAS LRS sources, and Hephaistos II (2024MNRAS.531..695S) fitted photosphere-plus-blackbody SEDs to ~5 million stars. Those works constrain a fixed-temperature excess population star by star using broadband WISE or IRAS data, whereas the card uses SPHEREx 0.75-5 um spectrophotometry and a T-versus-L population test.

closest_prior.relation: Set upper limits on the fraction of Gaia DR2 stars with fixed-temperature (100-1000 K) waste-heat excess using AllWISE colour cuts, but did not fit T_ex per source or test T against host luminosity.
Fitted 100-600 K blackbodies to IRAS LRS spectra over most of the sky and set Dyson-sphere upper limits, without analysing the T_ex distribution against host L.
Ran photosphere-plus-blackbody SED fits on ~5 million Gaia/2MASS/WISE sources to flag individual candidates, not a population T_ex-L scaling or a temperature-clustering test.
Built a data-driven W1/W2 excess catalogue of ~4.9 million FGK stars and reports fractional luminosities, but no excess-temperature-versus-luminosity analysis.

judge_output.what_would_make_it_open: Nothing on the card needs to change for its T_ex-versus-L statistic to be new; it would be fully open only if no prior work had constrained fixed-temperature (~300 K) excess populations, which Hephaistos I and Carrigan already did with WISE and IRAS.

judge_output.rationale: The natural half of the claim, that excess dust temperature rises with host mass or luminosity, has been tested at the population level. Chen et al. 2014 did this for about 500 Spitzer IRS warm-plus-cold debris disks, and Pawellek et al. 2014 did it for 34 Herschel-resolved cold disks. Neither tests the 3-5 um hot-excess population, fits a T proportional to L^alpha exponent, or searches for a luminosity-independent temperature spike. The waste-heat searches (Hephaistos I/II, Carrigan 2009) fit 100-1000 K blackbody components to individual sources or set prevalence limits, and none tests for a fixed-temperature cluster across host luminosity.

closest_prior.relation: Fit one- and two-temperature blackbodies to ~500 Spitzer IRS debris-disk excesses and found higher-mass stars host hotter grains, a related T-host trend but for 100-500 K zodiacal dust at 5-35 um, with no exponent fit or fixed-T clustering search.
Showed dust temperature rises toward earlier spectral types in 34 Herschel-resolved cold disks, the same kind of T-L dependence but in far-IR Kuiper-belt analogs rather than 3-5 um excesses.
Fit photosphere-plus-blackbody models to Gaia/2MASS/WISE excesses in ~5 million stars to flag individual waste-heat candidates, with no population test of excess temperature versus host luminosity.
Fit 100-600 K blackbodies to IRAS LRS spectra all-sky to find individual cloaked-star candidates and set upper limits, without examining clustering of fitted temperature across host luminosity.

judge_output.what_would_make_it_open: No listed work delivers the selection-corrected distribution of fitted 3-5 um excess temperature versus Gaia host luminosity across two decades in L, together with a kernel-density search for a host-independent temperature overdensity. The SPHEREx spectral excess catalog would supply this for the first time.

judge_output.rationale: The card measures the distribution of best-fit 3-5 um excess temperature against host luminosity for an all-sky population, using SPHEREx 0.75-5 um spectral shape, and tests whether any subpopulation clusters at a fixed temperature independent of L. Hephaistos I/II (2022MNRAS.512.2988S, 2024MNRAS.531..695S) and Carrigan (2009ApJ...698.2075C) searched for individual waste-heat candidates or set prevalence limits from WISE/IRAS photometry, which shows that an excess exists but cannot constrain the shape of a hot 3-5 um excess. None of them examined the T_ex-versus-L* population distribution. Chen et al. (2014ApJS..211...25C) and Pawellek et al. (2014ApJ...792...65P) found dust temperature rising with stellar mass or spectral type, but only for small, pre-selected debris-disk samples of cooler dust at wavelengths longer than 5 um, and they did not test for a host-independent temperature spike, so the card's population test is untested.

closest_prior.relation: Measured one- and two-temperature dust fits in Spitzer IRS (5-35 um) spectra of ~500 debris disks and found higher grain temperatures around higher-mass stars; this is a cooler, pre-selected population with no test for fixed-temperature clustering or 3-5 um excesses.

Ran SED fits of blackbody-plus-photosphere models to Gaia/2MASS/WISE photometry for 5 million stars to flag individual candidates; it did not measure the T_ex-versus-L* population distribution and had no 3-5 um spectral shape.
Set upper limits on the fraction of stars hosting 100-1000 K waste-heat excesses from Gaia-WISE colour cuts; it did not fit a temperature-luminosity relation or test for clustering.
Found dust temperature increasing toward earlier spectral types for 34 Herschel-resolved cold debris disks; this is far-IR cold dust in a tiny sample, not the 3-5 um excess population.
